title: Cellular Reproduction
standard_text: Cells reproduce by mitosis for growth and repair and by meiosis to make sex cells; organisms reproduce asexually or sexually. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 7, Quarter 2: Life Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 2: Life Science): the cell cycle, mitosis, asexual and sexual reproduction, meiosis and stem cells and specialization. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mitosis copies cells; meiosis makes sex cells.
key_sub: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents.
body_html:
How to think about it

In mitosis one cell divides into two identical cells with the same number of chromosomes. It is used for growth and repair, and for asexual reproduction, where one parent makes offspring that are genetically identical (binary fission, budding, runners, cuttings).

Meiosis makes sex cells (gametes) with half the number of chromosomes: 23 in humans. In sexual reproduction two gametes join at fertilization, so the offspring get a mix of genes from two parents. This variation helps a population survive change.

Example

A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. How many does a sperm cell have?

Meiosis halves the number.

Answer: 23

Example

A strawberry plant grows new plants from runners. What kind of reproduction is this?

Only one parent

Answer: asexual

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up mitosis and meiosis.
  • Thinking asexual offspring are different from the parent.
  • Thinking sexual reproduction is faster.

faq.q: What is an advantage of asexual reproduction?
faq.a: It is fast and needs only one parent.
If the environment changes, some individuals may have traits that help them survive.

items.q: Which stage comes right after metaphase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: What happens in prophase?
c: nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing
chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles
items.e: Prophase: chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form.

items.q: What happens in G₂ phase?
c: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing
the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles
chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells
items.e: G₂ phase: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing.

items.q: Which stage is this? Chromosomes condense and become visible; the nuclear membrane breaks down.
items.e: Prophase: Chromosomes condense and become visible; the nuclear membrane breaks down.

items.q: What forms the spindle in animal cells?
items.e: Plant cells form a spindle without centrioles.

items.q: Which stage is this? DNA is replicated during the S stage.
items.e: Interphase: DNA is replicated during the S stage.

items.q: What is the significance of mitosis?
c: creating genetic variation by crossing over
growth, repair and keeping the chromosome number the same
items.e: It replaces worn-out cells.

items.q: Which stage comes right after prophase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: Which stage comes right after interphase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: Which stage is this? Spindle fibers attach to the centromeres at the cell's middle line.
items.e: Metaphase: Spindle fibers attach to the centromeres at the cell's middle line.

items.q: Which stage is this? The chromosomes start to uncoil as new nuclear membranes appear.
items.e: Telophase: The chromosomes start to uncoil as new nuclear membranes appear.

items.q: Which stage is this? Two new nuclei form around the chromosomes at each end.
items.e: Telophase: Two new nuclei form around the chromosomes at each end.

items.q: Which stage comes right before prophase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: Which stage comes right after telophase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: Which division is called equational division?
items.e: The chromosome number stays the same.

items.q: Which stage is this? The cytoplasm splits and two daughter cells form.
items.e: Cytokinesis: The cytoplasm splits and two daughter cells form.

items.q: Which stage comes right before cytokinesis?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: What happens in metaphase?
c: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing
chromosomes line up at the equator (metaphase plate)
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
items.e: Metaphase: chromosomes line up at the equator (metaphase plate).

items.q: Which stage comes right before metaphase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: Which stage is this? Sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite ends of the cell.
items.e: Anaphase: Sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite ends of the cell.

items.q: A dog body cell has 78 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in each daughter cell after mitosis?
items.e: Mitosis makes identical cells with the same number.

items.q: Which division is called reductional division?
items.e: The chromosome number is halved.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 12 hours. In a sample, 24 of 500 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 24/500 × 720 min = 34.6 min.

items.q: A human cell with 46 chromosomes divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in both daughter cells together?
items.e: Two cells × 46 = 92.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 36 of 250 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 14.4%.

items.q: What is the G₀ phase?
c: a quiescent stage where cells stop dividing but stay metabolically active
items.e: e.g. heart cells.

items.q: At which stage are chromosomes best studied?
items.e: They are most condensed then.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 12 of 200 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 6.00%.

items.q: A mouse cell has 40 chromosomes. After DNA replication, how many sister chromatids are there?
items.e: Each chromosome is copied: 40 × 2 = 80.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing?
items.e: G₂ phase: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing.

items.e: S phase: DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles.

items.q: A corn body cell has 20 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in each daughter cell after mitosis?
items.e: Mitosis makes identical cells with the same number.

items.q: For mitosis, what is whether daughter cells are genetically identical?
c: in the testes and ovaries to make gametes
identical to each other and the parent
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: When does a recessive trait appear?
c: when an organism has two recessive alleles
when one recessive allele is present
items.e: For example, bb.

items.q: For meiosis, what is its role?
c: in the testes and ovaries to make gametes
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: What is one advantage of sexual reproduction?
c: Variation helps some offspring survive if the environment changes.
items.e: Variation is useful.

items.q: What is an allele?
c: a different version of the same gene
items.e: For example, B or b.

items.q: For mitosis, what is its role?
c: in the testes and ovaries to make gametes
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: What does a dominant allele do?
c: It shows its trait even when only one copy is present.
It needs two copies to show.
items.e: Shown by a capital letter.

items.q: Kristine reads: “Bees carry pollen so flowers make seeds.” How will the offspring's genetic information compare with the parent's?
c: It will be identical to one parent's.
It will be completely random with no parent genes.
It will be a mix of genes from two parents.
items.e: Asexual reproduction copies one parent's DNA; sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents.

items.q: For mitosis, what is the chromosome number of the daughter cells?
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: How many sets of chromosomes does a human get from each parent?
c: one set (23 chromosomes) from each parent

items.q: For meiosis, what is whether daughter cells are genetically identical?
c: in the testes and ovaries to make gametes
identical to each other and the parent
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: For mitosis, what is the number of daughter cells made?
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: Compare human sperm and eggs. For an egg cell, what is the food store?
c: large, one of the largest human cells
cytoplasm with a store of food for the early embryo
items.e: Sperm: small, many, swim, acrosome. Egg: large, few, food store, moved by cilia.

items.q: Compare human sperm and eggs. For an egg cell, what is the special feature at the front?
c: a jelly coat that changes after one sperm enters
cytoplasm with a store of food for the early embryo
an acrosome with enzymes to digest the egg's outer layer
items.e: Sperm: small, many, swim, acrosome. Egg: large, few, food store, moved by cilia.

items.q: Compare human sperm and eggs. For a sperm cell, what is the size?
c: large, one of the largest human cells
items.e: Sperm: small, many, swim, acrosome. Egg: large, few, food store, moved by cilia.

items.q: Compare human sperm and eggs. For a sperm cell, what is the number made?
c: a jelly coat that changes after one sperm enters
items.e: Sperm: small, many, swim, acrosome. Egg: large, few, food store, moved by cilia.

items.q: Jasmine reads: “A bacterium splits into two cells.” What type of reproduction is this?
items.e: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents (egg and sperm, or pollen and egg).

items.q: Compare human sperm and eggs. For an egg cell, what is the movement?
c: cannot move by itself; it is moved by cilia in the oviduct
an acrosome with enzymes to digest the egg's outer layer
items.e: Sperm: small, many, swim, acrosome. Egg: large, few, food store, moved by cilia.

items.q: For meiosis, what is where it happens in humans?
c: in body cells for growth and repair
in the testes and ovaries to make gametes
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: Kenneth reads: “Bees carry pollen so flowers make seeds.” What type of reproduction is this?
items.e: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents (egg and sperm, or pollen and egg).

items.q: What happens in anaphase I of meiosis?
c: homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together
sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits
chromosomes become visible as thin threads
homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents
items.e: Anaphase I: homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together.

items.q: Meiosis: number of cells produced?
items.e: Meiosis: four. Mitosis: two.

items.q: A fruit fly cell (2n = 8) finishes meiosis I. How many chromosomes are in each of the two new cells?
items.e: Homologs separate in meiosis I, so each cell has 4 (each still with two chromatids).

items.q: A mouse egg and sperm each have 20 chromosomes. How many does the fertilized egg have?
Mitosis: number of cells produced?
items.e: Meiosis: four. Mitosis: two.

items.q: How long does a typical human cell cycle take in culture?
items.e: Yeast takes only about 90 minutes.

items.q: Meiosis: main purpose?
items.e: Meiosis: making gametes for sexual reproduction. Mitosis: growth and repair.

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Homologous chromosomes separate to opposite poles.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: A human egg and sperm each have 23 chromosomes. How many does the fertilized egg have?
In which stage of meiosis does this happen: sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits?
items.e: Anaphase II: sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits.

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: chromosomes become visible as thin threads?
items.e: Leptotene: chromosomes become visible as thin threads.

items.q: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 23.

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: chiasmata terminalize and the nuclear envelope breaks down?
items.e: Diakinesis: chiasmata terminalize and the nuclear envelope breaks down.

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Single chromosomes line up in the middle of two cells.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: A chicken egg and sperm each have 39 chromosomes. How many does the fertilized egg have?
In which stage of meiosis does this happen: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen?
items.e: Diplotene: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen.

items.q: Meiosis: are the new cells identical?
items.e: Meiosis: no, genetically different. Mitosis: yes, identical.

items.q: Mitosis: chromosome number in new cells?
items.e: Meiosis: half (haploid). Mitosis: same (diploid).

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Homologous chromosomes pair up and swap pieces (crossing over).
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: A dog body cell has 78 chromosomes. How many homologous pairs is that?
How might high estrogen levels increase the risk of breast cancer?
c: estrogen can switch on genes that promote cell division
items.e: Fat tissue after the menopause makes estrogen.

items.q: What is cloning rare plants quickly and cheaply from meristems?
c: a current use of adult stem cells
a use of plant stem cells
a possible future use of stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: How does increased methylation of DNA affect a gene?
c: it stops transcription factors binding, so the gene is switched off
items.e: Methyl groups are added to cytosine.

items.q: What is a unipotent stem cell?
c: one that can become any cell
one that can only become one type of cell
items.e: For example cardiomyocytes from heart stem cells.

items.q: What is a transcription factor?
c: an enzyme that joins amino acids
a protein that binds to DNA and switches transcription of a gene on or off
items.e: It binds near the gene's promoter.

items.q: Why is it harder to find the proteome from the genome in complex organisms?
c: non-coding DNA and regulatory genes make it hard to predict the proteins
items.e: Alternative splicing also adds proteins.

items.q: Which statement about adult stem cells from bone marrow is true?
c: They can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life.
They can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells.
They can become almost any type of cell.
items.e: They are taken from the patient or a donor.

items.q: mRNA: AAAGGCGUU. Codons: AAA = Lys, GGC = Gly, GUU = Val, CUU = Leu, GGU = Gly. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: AAA GGC GUU.

items.q: Which statement about embryonic stem cells is true?
c: They can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells.
They can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life.
They can become almost any type of cell.
items.e: There are ethical objections because embryos are destroyed.

items.q: A stem cell in bone marrow becomes a red blood cell. Which process is this mainly?
items.e: Mitosis makes more cells; differentiation makes cells specialized.

items.q: Which type of stem cell can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells?
c: adult stem cells from bone marrow
items.e: They are taken from the patient or a donor.

items.q: What is the difference between benign and malignant tumors?
c: malignant tumors invade tissues and spread (metastasis)
benign tumors spread around the body
items.e: Benign tumors are usually enclosed.

items.q: What is growing crops with special features, such as disease resistance?
c: a use of plant stem cells
a possible future use of stem cells
a current use of adult stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: mRNA: CAAUUUAGC. Codons: AGC = Ser, CAA = Gln, UUU = Phe, CUU = Leu, GUU = Val. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: CAA UUU AGC.

items.q: A stem cell in the brain becomes a neuron. Which process is this mainly?
items.e: Mitosis makes more cells; differentiation makes cells specialized.

items.q: What is treating paralysis by replacing damaged nerve cells?
c: a current use of adult stem cells
a possible future use of stem cells
a use of plant stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: An embryo's cells become heart, nerve and skin cells. Which process is this mainly?
items.e: Mitosis makes more cells; differentiation makes cells specialized.

items.q: mRNA: CAUAAAAUU. Codons: AAA = Lys, AUU = Ile, CAU = His, GCU = Ala. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: CAU AAA AUU.

items.q: Which statement about meristem tissue in plants is true?
c: They can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life.
They can become almost any type of cell.
They can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells.
items.e: It is found at the tips of roots and shoots.

items.q: A lizard regrows a lost tail. Which process is this mainly?
items.e: Mitosis makes more cells; differentiation makes cells specialized.
